prompt_demand: State that an incompatible donor kidney would be rejected, so dialysis must continue to remove urea until a matching kidney is found.
reason: The answer is the taught account that a donor must match or the kidney is rejected, and that dialysis removes urea in the meantime. The patient detail does not call for any new inference. The operator's review classes generic transplant/dialysis comparisons and mechanisms as A, and this item fits that ruling.
uncertainty: medium: I would keep it as B if the teacher sees choosing between the two treatments for a stated patient condition as a genuine consequential inference (B5/B7).

prompt_demand: Outline the three dialysis principles and give the reason for each: urea diffuses into fluid that has no urea, blood cells are too large to cross, and the fluid's glucose concentration matches blood so there is no net loss.
reason: Each mark needs a causal reason (concentration gradient, particle size, equal concentration means no net diffusion), not a recalled name. That is taught understanding, so Understand fits better than Remember. The AO stays A.
uncertainty: low-medium: I would keep Remember if the bank's convention puts every FEATURE card at Remember whatever its reasoning content.

prompt_demand: Give the reason the second neurone stops responding when neurotransmitter release is blocked but the receptors still work.
reason: The prompt asks 'describe why' and the marks reward reasons, which is what the syllabus means by Explain, not Describe ('state the main points'). The AO2 label is sound because the learner has to reason through a modified mechanism. FLAG: changing the command word may change which tariff rules apply. Other AO2 explain APP cards in this group (for example 3-050 and 3-080) also carry 2 marks.
uncertainty: low on the mismatch; medium on whether the tariff rules for explain allow 2 marks on this card type.

prompt_demand: Give the reason route X (a reused syringe with another person's blood) carries more blood-borne infection risk than route Y (new sterile equipment).
reason: 'Describe why' asks for reasons, so Explain is the syllabus command word that fits. FLAG: this change may change the tariff rules. AO2 is kept but is a boundary: the reasoning is very close to the taught account in 3-102 (HIV passed on by shared needles), and a teacher could reasonably call it A.
uncertainty: low on the command word; medium-high on the AO, which I would move to AO1 if the teacher sees comparing X and Y as repeating 3-102 rather than an inference.

prompt_demand: Make a large, unshaded labelled drawing of a spinal cord transverse section from a photomicrograph, showing the grey matter, white matter and central canal.
reason: The workspace crosswalk counts drawing from a specimen as C, and similar photomicrograph drawings (3-129, 3-130, 3-226, 3-355) are AO3 Apply. One mark here is purely drawing quality. Against that, the approved plan classes this objective as A-taught, and three of the four marks reward a structure layout the learner could reproduce from memory. The heart drawing 3-386 is labelled the same way.
uncertainty: medium: I would move it to AO3/Apply if the teacher decides that marks for drawing from an image make it C2 whatever the objective. 3-386 should then be reviewed with it for consistency.

prompt_demand: Reason that because anaerobic respiration releases less energy per glucose molecule, a muscle with the same energy demand must break down more glucose per minute.
reason: The first mark is taught recall (3-025). The second needs a consequential step: if the demand stays fixed and the yield per glucose falls, the rate must rise. That step is modest but it is real reasoning, so B is defensible.
uncertainty: medium: I would move it to AO1 if the teacher regards 'more glucose is needed' as part of the taught aerobic/anaerobic comparison.

prompt_demand: Match two described responses (fast and brief versus blood-borne and lasting hours) to nervous or hormonal control.
reason: The learner has to pick out the features in the supplied descriptions and classify each one (B1/B4). However, the descriptions spell out the taught distinction from 3-088, so very little processing is needed.
uncertainty: medium: I would move it to AO1 if the teacher sees it as recognising the taught distinction rather than handling information.

prompt_demand: Decide which culture (bacteria or viruses inside animal cells) a cell-wall-blocking medicine affects, and give the reason.
reason: Applying a stated mode of action to two supplied cultures is a small inference. But the reasoning repeats the taught chain in 3-093 (antibiotics have no target in viruses), and the operator ruled that generic established features of viruses are A.
uncertainty: medium: I would move it to AO1 if the teacher treats it as the 3-093 taught account in a thin new setting.
